target_venues.name: Journal of Biomedical Informatics (JBI)
target_venues.scope_alignment: HIGH: JBI explicitly prioritizes novel methodologies that advance informatics principles, reproducible algorithms, and compositional architectures rather than pure empirical benchmark mining.
target_venues.word_limit: Typically 5,000–8,000 words (our manuscript is 3,987 words — optimal).
target_venues.figure_table_limits: No strict cap; 8 figures and 3 tables are standard for methodological papers.
target_venues.data_code_policy: Mandates data and code availability statement; open-source repositories highly favored.
target_venues.pros: Methodology-centric focus fits our core contribution (evidence synthesis + governance firewall).

target_venues.name: Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association (JAMIA)
target_venues.scope_alignment: HIGH: Focuses on clinical informatics, clinical ML rigor, reporting standards (TRIPOD+AI), and reproducible AI pipelines.
target_venues.word_limit: Typically 4,000 words for main text (our manuscript is 3,987 words — within boundary).
target_venues.figure_table_limits: Combined limit of 5–8 items (our 8 figures + 3 tables might require moving 3 figures/tables to online supplementary).
target_venues.data_code_policy: Strict compliance with TRIPOD+AI and open science statements.
target_venues.pros: High clinical prestige and wide readership among clinical informatics practitioners.
target_venues.cons: Tight word limit and strict limits on main-text display items.

recommendation.rationale: Our manuscript's primary scientific novelty is methodological (evidence synthesis, provenance boundaries, and architectural firewalls). JBI's formatting accommodates full 8-figure / 3-table display without truncating the audit evidence into supplementary files.
recommendation.secondary_target: JAMIA (as Research and Applications, moving Figures 3, 5, and Table 3 to Supplementary Material if display limit is enforced).
